title: Nourishing Gooey Dutch Potatoes Gratin
description: A comforting Dutch dish featuring new potatoes, mustard, and fermentation, perfect for a cold winter night. This recipe is raw-friendly and incorporates fermented ingredients for added nutrition.
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a large saucepan, combine the sliced potatoes and enough cold water to cover them, then bring to a boil over high heat.
Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer the potatoes for 5 minutes, or until they are slightly tender.
Drain the potatoes and set them aside.
In a large skillet, melt the butter over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion to the skillet and cook, stirring occasionally, until it is softened and lightly browned.
Add the minced garlic to the skillet and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Stir in the whole grain mustard, sauerkraut, salt, and black pepper.
In a greased 9x13 inch baking dish, create a layer of potatoes.
Spread half of the mustard-sauerkraut mixture over the potatoes, then sprinkle with half of the shredded gruyere cheese.
Repeat the layers, starting with the potatoes, then the remaining mustard-sauerkraut mixture, and finally the remaining gruyere cheese.
Cover the dish with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for an additional 20 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and the potatoes are tender.
